narration: Welcome to the Sculpture Gallery. Here we have the Kushan‑era Yaksha of Wealth, Kubera, accession number NM 64.9/1, a 61‑centimetre figure carved from spotted red sandstone in the 2nd century CE. The pot‑belly, heavily jewelled form sits in a relaxed royal pose, a visual bridge between earlier nature‑spirit cults and the later Hindu and Buddhist iconography that would come to dominate the region. This piece, found in Mathura, illustrates how folk deities were gradually woven into the mainstream pantheon as guardians of wealth and treasure. Enjoy exploring the intricate details that speak to the craftsmanship and spiritual symbolism of this remarkable artifact.
